latest.question: D'fhiafraigh Deputy Aengus Ó Snodaigh den Aire Forbartha Tuaithe agus Pobail, agus Gaeltachta cé mhéad go sonrach atá le baint ó bhuiséad caipitil na nOileán agus cé mhéad atá le baint ó bhuiséad caipitil na Gaeltachta sa chiorrú atá leagtha amach sa Bhuiséad ar airgead caipitil na Gaeltachta agus na nOileán ó €55,362,000 in 2026 go €50,362,000 in 2027.
latest.reply:
Tá leithdháileadh iomlán de €628 milliún faighte ag mo Roinn i gCáinaisnéis 2027, lena n-áirítear leithdháileadh caiptil de €273 milliún. Foilseofar leithdháileadh mionsonraithe de réir fomhír san Imleabhar Meastachán Athbhreithnithe (REV) roimh dheireadh na bliana.
Tá pleananna fíor-uaillmhianacha ag mo Roinn d'fhorbairtí caipitil chun tacú le pobail Ghaeltachta, pobal na Gaeilge agus pobail na n-oileán araon. Maoinítear na forbairtí seo as Clár C de bhuiséad na Roinne - An Ghaeltacht, an Ghaeilge agus na hOileáin. Is fiú a mheabhrú gur tháinig ardú ar an mbuiséad caipitil do Chlár C ó €30 milliún in 2025 go beagnach €55 milliún in 2026. Bhain cuid mhaith den ardú sin le trí phríomhthionscadal infreastruchtúir:
• Cé Inis Oírr,
• An tIonad Gaeilge agus Cultúir ar Shráid Fhearchair, agus
• athfhorbairt shuíomh Choláiste Lurgan in Indreabhán mar Ionad Oideachais agus Óige do Ghaeltacht Chonamara.
Rinneadh gealltanas i leith na dtionscadal seo sa Phlean Forbartha Náisiúnta, agus is cúis áthais dom an maoiniú a fháil chun iad a thabhairt i gcrích anois. Táim den tuairim mheáite go mbeidh an t-allúntas caipitil atá faighte ag mo Roinn leordhóthanach le freastal ar riachtanais chlár na Gaeltachta, na Gaeilge agus na nOileán i 2027 agus sna blianta ina dhiaidh sin.

latest.question: Deputy Pádraig O'Sullivan asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht if he will bring forward approvals for the current CCIF program for emergency cases.
latest.reply:
The Community Centre Investment Fund (CCIF) was introduced to provide high quality community facilities that are available to community groups in both urban and rural communities. Through the CCIF, some €112 million has been allocated for the enhancement and refurbishment of existing community centres and the construction of new centres where such a need has been identified.
I launched the latest round of funding under CCIF 2026 on the 26th March for enhancement and refurbishment of existing community centres. The fund will be delivered across 2 categories with maximum funding levels of €25,000 and €100,000 respectively. The closing date for the CCIF 2026 has now passed.
I am committed to ensuring the applications received are processed quickly. Applications are currently being assessed and I expect to announce the successful projects under category 1 which provides funding of up to €25,000 in the coming weeks with approvals under category 2 providing funding of up to €100,000 being announced before year-end.

latest.question: Deputy William Aird asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the timeline for the next round of applications for the Community Centre Investment Fund; the eligibility criteria; and the funding limits that will apply.
latest.reply:
The Community Centre Investment Fund (CCIF) was introduced to provide high quality community facilities that are available to community groups in both urban and rural communities. Through the CCIF, some €112 million has been allocated for the enhancement and refurbishment of existing community centres and the construction of new centres where such a need has been identified.
I launched the latest round of funding under CCIF 2026 on the 26th of March for enhancement and refurbishment of existing community centres. The fund will be delivered across 2 categories with maximum funding levels of €25,000 and €100,000 respectively. The closing date for the CCIF 2026 has now passed.
Applications are currently being assessed and I look forward to announcing the successful projects under category 1 which provides funding of up to €25,000 in the coming weeks with approvals under category 2 providing funding of up to €100,000 being announced before year-end.
I am committed to delivering further iterations of the scheme in the coming years in line with the commitment in the Programme for Government for this to become a permanent rolling fund. I have indicated previously that the 2027 scheme will focus on new build centres and the eligibility criteria and funding limits that will apply will be announced when that scheme is launched next year.

latest.question: Deputy William Aird asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht when the next round of the Local Enhancement Programme will be announced; and the level of funding that will be available for community groups.
latest.reply:
The Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) is targeted towards supporting communities that are impacted by disadvantage, as identified in the Local Economic and Community Plan (LECP) of the relevant local authority. It generally provides small capital grants to community and voluntary groups for the improvement/refurbishment of their facilities and/or the purchase of equipment. The fund is administered locally on behalf of the Department by Local Community Development Committees (LCDCs) across the country, with support from their local authority.
The Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) for 2026 provided €7 million in capital supports. Each LCDC decided the projects that were funded under LEP 2026. The closing date for community groups to submit applications for LEP 2026 was 27 February 2026 and the list of successful projects was announced on 2 July 2026. Therefore, the 2026 programme is now closed.
I was delighted to secure current funding of €2 million for the LEP in Budget 2027 to assist community organisations in easing the pressure of rising operating costs. This is in addition to €5 million in capital funding that is available for LEP 2027. My Department is currently considering the detailed design of the LEP for 2027 and I hope to announce the new programme before the end of this year.
The Department would encourage all community and voluntary organisations to check our website at www.gov.ie/drcdg, and to engage with their Local Community Development Committees (LCDCs), Local

latest.question: Deputy William Aird asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the level of funding remaining under the LEADER Programme 2023-2027; and the measures being taken to ensure that funding is fully utilised.
latest.reply:
The LEADER Programme is co-funded by the European Union and is delivered through Local Action Groups (LAGs) across rural Ireland. A feature of the LEADER programme is that it is based on a community-led, bottom-up approach to rural development.
The 2023-2027 LEADER programme has total funding of €180 million, with 75% or €135 million available to support projects being completed by rural groups and businesses.
The funding is allocated in advance to LAGs to provide them with greater flexibility to manage their budgets over the programming period. Funding is then paid out by my Department as costs are incurred and claims for payment are submitted.
Using this allocation, LEADER LAGs have approved funding of over €76.8 million for some 1,537 LEADER projects countrywide. This means that c. 57% of the overall project allocation is committed, with some €58 million or 43% remaining. Of these, 551 projects have been completed to date, with the remainder due to be completed over the coming months and years. There are an additional 172 projects progressing through the approval stages across all sub-regional areas.
The €180 million also includes €45 million (or 25%) which is available to support the administration and animation costs of the LAGs involved in running the programme. Of this, €20.1 million has been drawn down to date, with some €24.9 million remaining. latest.question: Deputy William Aird asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the funding allocated to the Social Inclusion and Community Action Programme (SICAP) for 2027.
latest.reply: The Social Inclusion and Community Activation Programme (SICAP) is Ireland's primary social inclusion programme, which aims to reduce poverty and promote social inclusion and equality by supporting disadvantaged individuals and communities across the country. The programme works with individuals and local community groups to address barriers to participation and strengthen community capacity. I am pleased to have secured almost €74 million for SICAP and other social inclusion supports in Budget 2027. Just under €65 million of that allocation is for SICAP providing greater long-term funding stability for the programme and enabling the continuation of important work across the country. It should be noted that the final estimated allocations for each area will be confirmed in the Revised Estimates Volume which will be published in December, and considered by the relevant select committees. A particularly welcome development is the provision of long-term funding certainty, with previously temporary funding for new arrivals made a permanent part of the core SICAP allocation. This represents an important step towards ensuring that community integration supports can be delivered on a more sustainable, long-term basis. This provides greater certainty for those planning and delivering services and helps sustain integration supports in communities. My Department remains committed to supporting this important work and ensuring that SICAP continues to respond to the needs of disadvantage

latest.question: Deputy Pat Buckley asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the new measures and funding that have been provided in Budget 2027 to address rural isolation and loneliness, particularly among older people and those living in remote communities.
latest.reply:
Budget 2027 has seen my Department’s allocation increase from €611 million to €628 million. This provides €208 million for rural development, almost €260 million for community development, and €161 million for the Gaeltacht, Irish language and the Islands.
The €208 million allocation for rural development will support programmes such as LEADER, the Rural Regeneration and Development Fund, Town and Village Renewal Scheme, CLÁR, Local Improvement Scheme and the Outdoor Recreation and Infrastructure Scheme. These programmes can help tackle isolation by supporting community facilities, local services and recreational activities, particularly in areas where distance and limited access to services can make it harder for people to stay connected.
The community development programme funding will fund targeted community supports including, for example, the Senior Alerts Scheme which helps older people live safely and independently in their own homes. Other important aspects of Budget 2027 for community development include:
• An additional €5 million for Community Services Programme, bringing the allocation to €64.4 million, to support community organisations delivering local services, including meals-on-wheels services.
• €74 million for social inclusion, including almost €65 million for the Social Inclusion and Community Activation Programme (SICAP), which supports disadvantaged individuals and communities to participate more fully in local life.
• Increase of €1 million for the SÍOL

latest.question: Deputy Liam Quaide asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht if his Department will provide dedicated capital funding to Cork County Council in 2027 for the planned development of community and recreational amenities, independently of grant schemes reliant on applications from voluntary community groups, particularly to address serious amenity deficits in rapidly growing settlements in east Cork.
latest.reply:
The broad range of funded schemes under my Department’s Rural Investment Programme are in the main made available to local authorities and community groups on the basis of applications being submitted in response to Calls for Proposals. This approach is designed to underpin effective delivery of high quality projects for rural communities, and sees applications assessed in a fair and consistent manner, informed by considerations such as suitability against scheme criteria, geographical spread and the quality of the projects.
The Rural Regeneration and Development Fund is a key element of the Rural Development Investment Programme which supports large-scale, ambitious capital projects that can achieve sustainable economic and social development in rural areas. The focus of the RRDF is on rural towns and villages with a population of less than 10,000 people. To date, it has allocated over €611 million to 271 projects located across the country, including over €43.2million to 27 projects in Co. Cork.
I was delighted to open a Call for Category 1 proposals under the Fund in February this year, which sought applications for strategically important, large-scale capital projects that have full planning and other consents in place and are ready to commence. latest.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the additional supports in place for social enterprises as a result of Budget 2027.
latest.reply:
The Government recognises the important contribution that social enterprises make to communities across Ireland by delivering social, environmental and economic benefits, while also creating employment opportunities and supporting inclusive local development.
My Department supports social enterprises under a number of different funding streams and I am pleased to note that these supports have been maintained or increased as a result of Budget 2027.
Regarding the delivery of Trading for Impact, the national social enterprise policy, a significant increase in funding to support this was delivered under Budget 2026, and I expect that this funding will remain unchanged. This will support a range of measures to deliver on the objectives of the policy, including verification of social enterprises, awareness and capacity building and impact measurement.
My Department's Community Services Programme (CSP) currently supports the delivery of 453 services nationally via 434 community organisations to provide local social, economic, and environmental services through a social enterprise model, with a budget of €59.4m in 2026. This Programme provides an annual co-funding contribution towards each full-time equivalent (FTE) position being supported and, where warranted, towards the cost of employing a manager. The CSP Programme currently provides funding towards 1,723 FTEs and 354 manager positions.

latest.question: Deputy Colm Burke asked the Minister for Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science the steps his Department is taking to assist students following the unexpected and immediate closure of a language college in Cork (details supplied) given that the abrupt closure of the college has left students who rely on it for their immigration status in a uncertain and distressing situation.
latest.reply:
My Department is aware of the closure of the English language education provider in question.
As a private provider, it does not come under the remit of my Department. Nor does my Department have a role in issues arising from a private contract between a student and a provider.
However, such a closure creates uncertainty which has a significant impact on the learners, prospective students, and staff of that provider.
For a provider to be eligible to recruit students from non-EEA countries, the provider’s courses must be included on the Interim List of Eligible Programmes (ILEP). The ILEP is administered by the Department of Justice, Home Affairs and Migration in conjunction with my Department. The provider in question was an ILEP listed provider.
ILEP listed providers are required to have arrangements in place for the protection of enrolled learners. These arrangements are to protect learners in the event that a provider fails, closes or is unable to deliver an ILEP-listed programme. In this case, the provider has had arrangements in place via an insurance product with Arachas.
The provider has been in contact with Quality and Qualifications Ireland (QQI) and advised that arrangements are being made to place learners with other providers in Cork and Dublin to enable them to complete their studies. Learners will be contacted by the provider directly.

latest.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science if he is concerned that TUD has decided to close its creche in the Tallaght campus; if he is concerned that students may have to drop out as a consequence; and if he will intervene with TUD to put the case for keeping the creche open.
latest.reply:
I thank the Deputy for his question about a creche closure on the grounds of TU Dublin's Tallaght campus. I am sure it is very disappointing news for those who avail of the service.
Regarding the particular case of the creche close on TU Dublin's Tallaght campus, this is a matter for the University and is not within the remit of my Department to intervene in such matters. As you no doubt are aware, TU Dublin operates with institutional autonomy in academic and administrative matters, including the operation of childcare facilities, as afforded to all publicly funded institutions under the Higher Education Authority Act, 2022.
I would strongly encourage students to engage directly with the university regarding any negative impacts of the closure.
As Minister, I am acutely aware of the need to provide a flexible, responsive tertiary system that is cognisant of the needs and responsibilities of students in our higher education institutions. examples.reply:
As previously advised to the Deputy, the school referred to was approved to enter my Department's pipeline of projects under the Additional School Accommodation (ASA) scheme.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.reply:

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
